referents.why: 'stretch out' belongs to the words Moses is told to say to Aaron, so the implied you is Aaron.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: 'strike' is in the same commanded words; the implied you is Aaron.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: the weqatal 'it will become gnats' is third masculine singular; the thing struck, the dust (w15), is what becomes gnats. The act decides, not the nearest noun.

links.why: cl0 is the frame of God's speech and comes before the commanded clauses; cl3 is inside the speech, so a then-link back to the frame is backward and crosses the speech boundary.
plain waw joining two commands at one level; the conjunction supports it.
the weqatal says what the command brings about; that is the result link, not a plain sequence.
imperative, then waw + third-person weqatal saying what will come of it (R4).
God says, and what is said is the clause 'say to Aaron' (R1).
'say to Aaron' introduces a collection of commands joined by waw; content points at the imperative group (R1).

groups.why: God (the LORD) speaks to Moses; the commanded turn is nested as a part (speech nests), so cl1 is the frame of turn1 rather than a separate part of God's turn.

groups.why: the commanded words are spoken by Moses, the one commanded to speak them, to Aaron (R2); the sender was a slot and is replaced by the candidate Moses.
commands joined by 'and' at one level are one imperative group with several command members; the weqatal is its effect.
absorbed into imp2: a second imperative group for cl3 breaks the one-level collection, and 'part' is not an imperative role.

referents.why: 'they did so' is plural and fulfils the command chain, which was addressed to Moses (to tell) and Aaron (to act); the composite Moses and Aaron is the only plural candidate that fits.

referents.why: 'he struck the dust' continues Aaron's acts in cl1 with no change of subject; the implied subject is Aaron.

links.why: a narrative 'did so' with no named subject after the command collection fulfils the whole collection (R4).

cl3 gives the detail of the summary report cl0.
cl4 restates the effect ('became gnats throughout the land of Egypt') in the command's own words.
cl4 gives the detail of the summary report cl0.

cant_tell.why: both repeat the verb hayah of the effect; both are recorded as fulfilling it, and the split between the gnats on man and beast (result of the striking) and the all-dust summary is not settled by the text.
the gloss gives a feminine singular verb while the gnats are masculine; no slot depends on it, since the subject is named as the gnats.

referents.why: 'their secret arts' belongs to the magicians, who are the doers of cl0; masculine plural agrees.
referents.category: possessive of the acting group

referents.why: 'they were not able' is third common plural, the same doers as cl0, the magicians.
referents.category: implied subject of a failed attempt

links.why: lamed + infinitive construct saying what the act was done to achieve: to bring forth the gnats.
the attempt, with a purpose, followed by 'and' + a negated verb of ability is the attempt's failed_result, which replaces the plain and.
an attempt with a purpose, then 'and' + a negated verb of being able: the attempt's outcome failed.
wayyiqtol continuing the narrative line after the failure.
this verse has only cl0 to cl3; cl4 is a clause of an earlier verse, and a then-link across verses is not a link type here.
'did thus' (ken) with a named subject, the magicians, who were not commanded: imitation of the deed just done after the latest command, the striking of the dust (not fulfilment).

referents.why: 'this is the finger of God': the demonstrative refers to the gnats just produced, which is not among the candidates. The feminine pronoun agrees with the predicate 'finger' (copula use), so the finger is not its referent.
referents.category: demonstrative whose referent is not a candidate

referents.why: 'he did not listen to them': the them are the magicians who had spoken; masculine plural agrees.

referents.why: the one who does not listen is a person, Pharaoh; the heart (w11) is what was hardened, not the listener. The act decides, so the builder's heart is replaced.

links.why: cl0 is the magicians' speech frame and comes before cl2 and cl3; the refusal is not a sequence after the frame.
waw joining the hardening of the heart and the refusal; the conjunction supports it.
cl1 is inside the magicians' speech; the narrative line continues from the speech frame cl0, which is the nearest clause not inside a speech.
ka'asher 'just as' before a clause nested in cl3's prepositional role: as the LORD had said.
the magicians say; what is said is the clause 'this is the finger of God' (R1).
wayehezaq continues the narrative line after the speech frame, which is the nearest clause before it not inside a speech.

groups.why: the magicians speak to Pharaoh; cl1 is the part said.

referents.why: 'say to him': the him is Pharaoh, to whom Moses is sent (cl2, before Pharaoh).

referents.why: 'that they may serve me' is in the LORD's quoted words; first person is the speaker, the LORD.

links.why: cl3 is inside God's speech and cl0 is its frame, which comes first; a then-link back to the frame is backward and crosses the speech boundary.
waw joining two commands at one level; the conjunction supports it.

an imperative followed by waw + a yiqtol in a different person is a purpose, not a plain and (rule for purpose).
'let my people go, so that they may serve me': command, then waw + yiqtol in third person plural, which looks forward to the aim.
God says, and the first thing said is a collection of commands joined by waw (R1).

links.why: 'thus says the LORD' introduces a collection of commands with its aim; content points at the imperative group (R1).

groups.why: God (the LORD) speaks to Moses; the commanded turn for Moses to deliver is nested as a part, and the setting clause cl3-cl4 sits in God's speech.

groups.why: 'rise early' and 'present yourself' are commands joined by waw at one level, one group with two command members; 'part' is not an imperative role.

groups.why: the innermost turn is the LORD's quoted words to Pharaoh, so the sender is the LORD; the builder had no addressee and the part is the imperative group.
